turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on through, Mr Keane. I'll grab your readings before the doctor sees you. Sleeve up there.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Right so. I'm not the best, a bit wobbly on the legs.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 104 over 68, pulse 96, temperature 37.1, and your oxygen is 98 percent. Lips are a little dry. He's free now, on you go.
[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thanks. I'm Nuala, I live in with him. He's been up and down to the toilet all night.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the computer's crawling on me. Mr Keane? What's brought you in?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. The runs. And getting sick. It was after the wedding.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Say that again, the screen jumped. The diarrhoea, was it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Diarrhoea and vomiting, after the meal at my niece's wedding.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Galway, Saturday. Salmon and some chicken thing. He's been bad since that feed.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): How many times have you been going?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe six or seven yesterday. Could have been eight. All watery, I lost count.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Nearer ten, I'd say. He was in and out constantly. He can't keep a count.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't think so. Just brown water.
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No blood, and nothing black. I checked.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is the vomiting still going on?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturday night I was sick a few times. Today, I don't know. I don't think I was.
[SEG0018] person_3 (CAREGIVER): You were, Paddy, once this morning. Not a lot, but you were sick in the bathroom. You've forgotten.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Was I? I don't know, doctor. Maybe I was, so.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the tummy?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Cramps, low down. Not terrible. They ease a bit after I go.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, where are the cramps? That beeped right over you.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Low down in the belly. They come and go.
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's hardly drinking. His mouth is dry, and he's only passed water once since yesterday morning.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm wrecked. No energy in me at all.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is anyone else from that wedding ill?
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His brother, and two cousins. Same thing, the runs and vomiting. They were texting this morning.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. I'll send a stool sample off today, and I'll give you a script for an anti-sickness tablet.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I don't know. Whatever you say.
[SEG0030] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Hold on, doctor. The chemist told him not to take the Imodium, in case it was a bug off the food. He took the green capsules anyway.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): He took what? Say that again, I was half reading the screen.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): The little green ones, for the runs. I don't know the dose. Maybe just the one capsule, a couple of times.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's Imodium, the loperamide. He took two capsules at lunch and two again in the evening. The chemist had said leave them.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): And your usual medicines?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): The water tablet in the morning. And a small white tablet for the blood pressure. I don't know the name of that one, doctor.

[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The water tablet is furosemide, forty milligrams, every morning, for the heart failure and the swollen ankles. The white one, we can't read the label. One every morning, for the blood pressure. He's had the pressure years.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I don't think so.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No. No allergies to anything.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): And how long has the diarrhoea been going, exactly?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days, I think. I don't know. Maybe I only properly noticed it Sunday.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Friday night, after the meal. He was up at three. That's four days, not two.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Four? I don't know, doctor. I get mixed up.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): So somewhere between two and four days. We'll not pin it harder than that. Bear with me, this thing's frozen. Long spin in, was it?
[SEG0045] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Desperate. Rain the whole way from Naas, then a crash on the M50, crawling.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I had the hurling on the phone in the traffic. Kilkenny were flying. I don't know the score in the end.

[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Grand match, only the weather ruined it. His grandson Cian was to be at the wedding and the flight was delayed, so the child missed the lot. He's eight in the winter and mad for the hurling.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Fierce disappointed, the poor lad. I don't know, he was nearly crying on the phone.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Kilkenny will do that to you. Right, the screen's back. Tongue is dry. Belly is soft, tender low down, no guarding, bowel sounds are busy.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'd call that mild dehydration, nothing dramatic.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Am I bad, doctor? I don't know.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): I don't think so. Working idea is gastroenteritis from the wedding food, what with the rest of them sick the same way. I can't name the bug.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Actually, scratch the stool sample for today, and forget the anti-sickness script. Too many of ye down from the one meal, and no blood, so I'm not sending it now.
[SEG0054] person_3 (CAREGIVER): So nothing gets sent?
[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): We might send a stool sample if it hasn't settled in three days, or sooner if you see blood. Not booking it today.

[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): Stop the Imodium. Hold the furosemide, the water tablet, until you're drinking properly. Keep the white blood pressure tablet going, we can't name it to stop it. Sip fluids little and often, water or flat lemonade.

[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): Get Dioralyte from the chemist, one sachet in a glass of water after each loose stool. If you can't keep fluids down, or you're getting worse, come back sooner. If it's not settled in three days, come back and we'll send that sample.
